body: Is the precedent here correct? Should `AWS_REGION` not be prefered if both `AWS_REGION` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` are both set?
Would it be better to have separate segments for the `profile` and the `region`?

My personal preference would be to have the profile then the region rather than the region then the profile.

```suggestion
                (Some(profile), Some(region)) => Some(format!("{}({})", profile, region)),
```
Actually, referring to https://github.com/aws/aws-cli/issues/735, `aws-cli` does not use `AWS_REGION` at all.
But I will keep `AWS_REGION` at lowest precedence because I heard some of the AWS-related programs are still using `AWS_REGION` env var.

This whole `if` can be replaced if you use the `?` operator on lines 52 & 53:

```
let aws_profile = env::var("AWS_PROFILE").ok()?;
let aws_region = get_aws_region_from_config(&aws_profile)?;
Some((aws_profile, aws_region))
```

(Note I didn't try to compile this, but it should be fairly close)

This is a bit of a hint that your return type is wrong. It seems like profile should be an `Option`.

I suspect you could neaten the whole module up with a struct:
```
struct AwsStatus {
    profile: Option<String>,
    region: Option<String>,
}
```
This is different semantic. I meant to return None when `aws_region` AND `aws_region` is both None.
In line 92 and 93, we need to make `SegmentConfig` which takes `&str`. If it is Option, we need to `unwrap_or_default` anyway.
Ok, yes - I see there is a slight difference. If you think the distinction is important, then you can leave it as-is.
